502-desert-gold.title: A Romance Of The Border
502-desert-gold.creator: Unknown
502-desert-gold.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Then a sharp clink of metal on stone and soft pads of hoofs in sand prompted Cameron to reach for his gun, and to move out of the light of the waning campfire. He was somewhere along the wild border line between Sonora and Arizona; and the prospector who dared the heat and barrenness of that region risked other dangers sometimes as menacing.

arxiv-2104-00713.title: Refined open topological strings revisited
arxiv-2104-00713.creator: Shi Cheng, and Piotr Sułkowski
arxiv-2104-00713.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Shi Cheng, and Piotr Sułkowski. In this work we verify consistency of refined topological string theory from several perspectives. First, we advance the method of computing refined open amplitudes by means of geometric transitions. Based on such computations we show that refined open BPS invariants are non-negative integers for a large class of toric Calabi-Yau threefolds: an infinite class of strip geometries, closed topological vertex geometry, and some threefolds with compact four-cycles.

arxiv-2106-01231.title: RX J0123.4-7321 - the story continues: major circumstellar disk loss and recovery. 2021 RX J0123.4-7321 - the story continues: major circumstellar disk loss and recovery. – References
arxiv-2106-01231.creator: M. J. Coe, A. Udalski, J. A. Kennea, P. A. Evans
arxiv-2106-01231.description: Abstract RX J0123.4-7321 is a well-established Be star X-ray binary system (BeXRB) in the Small Magellanic Cloud (SMC). Like many such systems the variable X-ray emission is driven by the underlying behaviour of the mass donor Be star. Previous work has shown that the optical and X-ray were characterised by regular outbursts at the proposed binary period of 119 d.

arxiv-2106-07383.title: Field Theory of Free Run and Tumble Particles in d d Dimensions
arxiv-2106-07383.creator: Ziluo Zhang, Gunnar Pruessner
arxiv-2106-07383.description: Abstract In this paper, Doi-Peliti field theory is used to describe the motion of free Run and Tumble particles in arbitrary dimensions. After deriving action and propagators, the mean square displacement and the corresponding entropy production at stationarity are calculated in this framework. We further derive the field theory of free Active Brownian Particles in two dimensions for comparison.

arxiv-2206-07256.title: Noise Covariance Estimation in Multi-Task High-dimensional Linear Models
arxiv-2206-07256.creator: Kai Tan, Gabriel Romon, Pierre C Bellec
arxiv-2206-07256.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Kai Tan, Gabriel Romon, Pierre C Bellec. This paper studies the multi-task high-dimensional linear regression models where the noise among different tasks is correlated, in the moderately high dimensional regime where sample size n n and dimension p p are of the same order. Our goal is to estimate the covariance matrix of the noise random vectors, or equivalently the correlation of the noise variables on any pair of two tasks.

arxiv-2207-13780.title: Star clusters in the Matching, Morse, and Generalized Morse complex
arxiv-2207-13780.creator: Connor Donovan, Nicholas A. Scoville
arxiv-2207-13780.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Connor Donovan, Nicholas A. Scoville. In this paper, we determine the homotopy type of the Morse complex and matching complex of multiple families of complexes by utilizing star cluster collapses and the Cluster Lemma. We compute the homotopy type of the Morse complex of an extended notion of a star graph, as well as the homotopy type of the matching complex of a Dutch windmill graph.

arxiv-2311-15197.title: Spin polarization and spin alignment from quantum kinetic theory with self-energy corrections
arxiv-2311-15197.creator: Shuo Fang, Shi Pu, Di-Lun Yang
arxiv-2311-15197.description: Abstract We derive the quantum kinetic theory for massive fermions with collision terms and self-energy corrections based on quantum field theory. We adopt an effective power counting scheme with ℏ \hbar expansion to obtain the leading-order perturbative solutions of the vector and axial Wigner functions and the corresponding kinetic equations.

arxiv-2405-13861.title: Transformers Can Learn Temporal Difference Methods for In-Context Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2405-13861.creator: Jiuqi Wang, Ethan Blaser, Hadi Daneshmand, Shangtong Zhang
arxiv-2405-13861.description: Abstract Traditionally, reinforcement learning (RL) agents learn to solve new tasks by updating their neural network parameters through interactions with the task environment. However, recent works demonstrate that some RL agents, after certain pretraining procedures, can learn to solve unseen new tasks without parameter updates, a phenomenon known as in-context reinforcement learning (ICRL).

arxiv-2503-02114.title: Fairness and/or Privacy on Social Graphs
arxiv-2503-02114.creator: Bartlomiej Surma, Michael Backes, Yang Zhang
arxiv-2503-02114.description: Abstract Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have shown remarkable success in various graph-based learning tasks. However, recent studies have raised concerns about fairness and privacy issues in GNNs, highlighting the potential for biased or discriminatory outcomes and the vulnerability of sensitive information.

arxiv-2506-19788.title: Line ratio identification of external photoevaporation 2026 Line ratio identification of external photoevaporation – A
arxiv-2506-19788.creator: Tyger Peake, Thomas J. Haworth, Mari-Liis Aru, William J. Henney
arxiv-2506-19788.description: Abstract External photoevaporation of protoplanetary discs, by massive O stars in stellar clusters, is thought to be a significant process in the evolution of a disc. It has been shown to result in significant mass loss and disc truncation, ultimately reducing the lifetime of the discs, and possibly affecting potential planet populations.

arxiv-2507-00736.title: Ordinality in Discrete-level Question Difficulty Estimation: Introducing Balanced DRPS and OrderedLogitNN
arxiv-2507-00736.creator: Arthur Thuy, Ekaterina Loginova, Dries F. Benoit
arxiv-2507-00736.description: Abstract Recent years have seen growing interest in Question Difficulty Estimation (QDE) using natural language processing techniques. Question difficulty is often represented using discrete levels, framing the task as ordinal regression due to the inherent ordering from easiest to hardest.

arxiv-2507-08453.title: Coarse Graining Photo-Isomerization Reactions: Thermodynamic Consistency and Implications for Molecular Ratchets
arxiv-2507-08453.creator: Francesco Avanzini, Massimiliano Esposito, Emanuele Penocchio
arxiv-2507-08453.description: Abstract We formulate thermodynamically consistent coarse-graining procedures for molecular systems undergoing thermally and photo-induced transitions: starting from elementary vibronic transitions, we derive effective photo-isomerization reactions interconverting ground-state species. Crucially, the local detailed balance condition, that constrains reaction kinetics to thermodynamics, remains satisfied throughout the coarse-graining procedures.

arxiv-2509-05070.title: Enriched bi(co)ends
arxiv-2509-05070.creator: Nicola Carissimi
arxiv-2509-05070.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Nicola Carissimi. In this paper we introduce the theory of ends and coends in the context of enriched bicategories. This will be an enriched version of the theory introduced in [ Cor16 ] , and a bicategorical version of the classical theory of enriched (co)ends, which can be found in [ Kel05 ] or in the more recent [ Lor21 ] .

arxiv-2512-02202.title: Progress in quantum metrology and applications for optical atomic clocks
arxiv-2512-02202.creator: Raphael Kaubruegger \orcidID 0000-0003-0846-2333 and Adam M. Kaufman \orcidID 0000-0003-4956-5814
arxiv-2512-02202.description: Abstract Quantum entanglement offers powerful opportunities for enhancing measurement sensitivity beyond classical limits, with optical atomic clocks serving as a leading platform for such advances. This chapter introduces the principles of entanglement-enhanced quantum metrology and explores their applications to timekeeping.

pmc-10610445.creator: Ju Wang, Marco Viola, Claudia Migliorini, Luca Paoletti, Silvia Arpicco, Chiara Di Meo, Pietro Matricardi, Duncan Craig
pmc-10610445.description: Nanocarriers have been extensively developed in the biomedical field to enhance the treatment of various diseases. However, to effectively deliver therapeutic agents to desired target tissues and enhance their pharmacological activity, these nanocarriers must overcome biological barriers, such as mucus gel, skin, cornea, and blood-brain barriers.

pmc-11541209.title: In vivo imaging of the human brain with the Iseult 11.7-T MRI scanner
pmc-11541209.creator: Nicolas Boulant, Franck Mauconduit, Vincent Gras, Alexis Amadon, Caroline Le Ster, Michel Luong, Aurélien Massire, Christophe Pallier, Laure Sabatier, Michel Bottlaender, Alexandre Vignaud, Denis Le Bihan
pmc-11541209.description: The understanding of the human brain is one of the main scientific challenges of the twenty-first century. In the early 2000s, the French Atomic Energy Commission launched a program to conceive and build a human magnetic resonance imaging scanner operating at 11.7 T. We have now acquired human brain images in vivo at such a magnetic field.

pmc-11658949.title: Pro-inflammatory and hyperinsulinaemic dietary patterns are associated with specific gut microbiome profiles: a TwinsUK cohort study
pmc-11658949.creator: Ni Shi, Sushma Nepal, Rachel Hoobler, Cristina Menni, Mary C Playdon, Daniel Spakowicz, Philippa M Wells, Claire J Steves, Steven K Clinton, Fred K Tabung
pmc-11658949.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Metabolic dietary patterns, including the Empirical Dietary Index for Hyperinsulinaemia (EDIH) and Empirical Dietary Inflammatory Pattern (EDIP), are known to impact multiple chronic diseases, but the role of the colonic microbiome in mediating such relationships is poorly understood. Among 1,610 adults with faecal 16S rRNA data in the TwinsUK cohort, we identified the microbiome profiles for EDIH and EDIP (from food frequency questionnaires) cross-sectionally using elastic net regression.

pmc-11691195.description: Altered mitochondrial function in aging skeletal muscle leads to elevated oxidative stress, reduced substrate oxidation and energy maintenance that contribute to decreased skeletal muscle mass, specific force and increased fatty infiltration and frailty with age. Metabolic flexibility in response to increased energy demand is a critical component of the mitochondrial adaptive response to muscle contraction.

pmc-13667985.title: Natural products modulate social behavior and gut microbiota in a valproic acid-induced zebrafish model of autism spectrum disorder
pmc-13667985.creator: Oana-Georgiana Oprea, Ioana-Miruna Balmus, Tudor Ilie, Gabriel Plavan, Mircea Nicusor Nicoara, Lucian Gorgan, Anca Trifan, Bogdan Stoica, Bogdan-Ionel Tamba, Alin Ciobica, Mitica Ciorpac
pmc-13667985.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Natural products rich in honey- and plant-derived bioactive compounds are increasingly investigated as modulators of the gut–brain–microbiome axis, a pathway implicated in autism spectrum disorder (ASD)-related behavioral and gastrointestinal alterations. This study evaluated whether two novel formulations, a honey-based product (API) and a plant extract-based product (MOD), modulate exploratory, anxiety-like, and social behavior and intestinal microbiota composition in an adult valproic acid (VPA)-induced zebrafish model of ASD.
